articles.title: Caroline Harvey hits hat-trick as ruthless USA put 11 past Austria at hockey worlds
articles.summary: Caroline Harvey scores three as unbeaten USA cruise. Hilary Knight extends worlds record to 70 goals. Canada thrash hosts Denmark 10-0 to stay perfect. Caroline Harvey scored a hat trick as defending champions the United States routed Austria 11-1 at the women’s ice hockey world championship on…
body: Canada followed suit by thrashing hosts Denmark 10-0 to maintain their own perfect record.
Austria’s late goal was the first conceded in three games by the US, who have scored 23 goals so far.

Tessa Janecke scored twice and added an assist, captain Hilary Knight netted twice, Joy Dunne had a goal and three assists, and Rory Guilday, Lacey Eden and Megan Keller each contributed a goal and an assist.
Harvey scored two of the opening period’s four goals and completed her hat trick in the third after registering five assists in her previous two games. She added another assist on Monday.

articles.title: Cricket Australia rules out reopening ball tampering investigation in wake of Khawaja book claims
articles.summary: No ‘compelling reason’ to establish another inquiry into incident. Usman Khawaja says ‘this has never been about commercial gain’ Cricket Australia will not reopen the investigation into the 2018 ball tampering controversy reignited by the release this week of Usman Khawaja’s book, which alleged…
body: Captain Steve Smith, vice-captain David Warner and batter Cameron Bancroft were handed long bans following a short Cricket Australia investigation into the incident.
Khawaja alleged more than those three players were aware of the team’s ball-tampering, and that his calls for the players to take collective responsibility at the time were rebuffed.

Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg told SEN radio on Tuesday there was not “any compelling reason” to revisit the investigation, even though there are “specific details” in Khawaja’s book “that contradict the versions that have been provided by others”.
Greenberg only stepped into his role last year, but was chief executive of the Australian Cricketers Association in 2021 when Bancroft told the Guardian he “lost control of [his] values”.

articles.title: CF Montreal are for sale: What it means, how much it could cost, and what’s next for the MLS club
articles.summary: In an emotional press conference, CF Montreal’s founder and owner Joey Saputo refused to rule out relocation. In a rare press conference, CF Montreal owner Joey Saputo announced that his family was beginning the process of “initiating a structured sale process” of the MLS club.
body: “This decision is neither driven by urgency, nor dictated by circumstance,” Saputo said in his initial scripted remarks. “It’s the result of a careful and deliberate reflection on where we stand today, and more importantly, on the opportunities that lie ahead for the club.”

Throughout his statement, Saputo stressed his desire to keep the club in Montreal, saying he hoped to find someone who “shares commitment to Montreal and who will ensure that the club remains in the city for many years to come.”
Yet, more than half an hour into the event after the floor was open for in-person questions, Saputo refused to rule out selling to a buyer who might move the club.

“I will not discount the club to the point of just giving it away just for the sake of giving it away,” Saputo said. “I want to be perfectly clear. I love this club. I will love this club to stay here. But if an owner comes in that doesn’t have the capacity to keep the club at the level that it needs to be at, and to spend the money that needs to be spent in order to bring in the players that this city wants to see, then at that point I’m not doing anyone a favor by selling it to someone just to keep it here.

articles.title: Warriors' Will Richard hoping that thumb injury won't require surgery
articles.summary: If Will Richard can play, he will. In a rough twist of fate for the Golden State Warriors ' second-year wing, Richard's left-thumb ulnar collateral ligament (UCL) tear - as revealed in the team's injury report Sunday night - came on a simple box-out in Saturday's overtime win over Orlando.
body: Conventional wisdom, given such a full tear, might suggest immediate corrective surgery.

"We're trying to wait until the swelling goes down," Richard said Monday, while squeezing a red grip device in his left hand. "Do a workout, catching, going full speed and all that, see if it's comfortable.
"But if I feel comfortable and confident, I want to play," he continued. "I want to be out there for the guys."

There are two typical paths in the event of a UCL tear in the thumb, said Dr. David Hay, an orthopedic surgeon and hand and wrist specialist in Los Angeles. If the joint remains stable, an athlete could return to play as soon as swelling decreases and a capable external stabilizer is found. If the joint is deemed unstable, though, the most obvious path is surgery, which - utilizing what's called "suture augmentation" - could get Richard back to playing within four to six weeks, Hay said.

articles.title: Initiative launched to make UK world leader in women's sport
articles.summary: The FA, Team GB and England Netball are among major organisations to back the Equal Sport Project - a new initiative aimed at improving equality and making the UK world leaders for women and girls' sport.
body: Recent research by Sporting Insights found that fewer than 1% of women working in sport believe gender equality has been achieved across the industry, while more than half believe they are paid less than men for carrying out the same role.

Several organisations have already made pledges based on the above, including Aquatics GB and the FA prioritising female leadership programmes, while Sport England and UK Sport have committed to working with their funding partners to ensure their governance is designed by men and women, for men and women.

The Youth Sport Trust, meanwhile, has committed to support schools in recognising and challenging stereotypes as well as develop male allies to champion gender equality in PE, school sport and physical activity.
The project is also backed by the UK government, with sports minister Stephanie Peacock saying: "We have seen progress in women and girls' sport, but there is still a long way to go.

articles.title: Bills defense turns tables on Vikings in victory
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills turned the tables on the Minnesota Vikings on Monday, producing a steely defensive performance on the road to grab a 23-6 victory in Minneapolis. A low-scoring showdown between the Bills' potent offense and the stingiest defense in the NFL ended with a hard-fought Buffalo victory…
body: Buffalo's defense proved decisive in the win, restricting the Vikings to just two field goals on a miserable night for Minnesota quarterback Carson Wentz.
Veteran back-up Wentz, starting in place of the injured Kyler Murray, struggled throughout, tossing two interceptions, coughing up a fumble and recording just eight completions.
The Bills offense dug deep to grind out victory, with running back James Cook rushing for 107 yards from 31 carries.
Bills quarterback Josh Allen threw 234 yards with one touchdown from 21 completions.

articles.title: Carrick position increasingly in doubt as hierarchy mulls over his future
articles.summary: Michael Carrick's position as Manchester United head coach is looking increasingly in doubt, but Sky Sports News has been told as yet, no final decision has been taken about his future.
body: As reported earlier on Monday, the club is carrying out a full review of the team's performance so far this season, led by director of football Jason Wilcox, with a plan for a decision to be made before the end of this international break.
Carrick was given a reprieve following the 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth a fortnight ago, with the bosses keen to give him a further three matches to try to turn the team's fortunes around.

But the pressure has continued to mount on Carrick after an eighth straight Premier League match without a win. There are now real doubts about whether he will be in charge of the team which goes to Anfield to play Liverpool the weekend after next.
The United hierarchy is determined that results have to improve, but they want to be sure about which direction to take the team before any action is taken.

articles.title: NI's O'Neill ruled out of Nations League matches
articles.summary: Arsenal forward Ceadach O'Neill is ruled out of Northern Ireland's final two Nations League fixtures against Ukraine in Belfast and Hungary in Budapest.
body: Arsenal forward Ceadach O'Neill has withdrawn from the Northern Ireland squad for the forthcoming Nations League matches against Ukraine and Hungary because of injury.
O'Neill won his first senior cap against Guinea in June and came on as a late substitute in the Nations League wins over Georgia and Ukraine in the last international window.

The 18-year-old, who now has four international caps, recently made his first senior appearance for Arsenal, starting in the Carabao Cup last-16 tie against Fleetwood Town, which the Gunners lost in a penalty shootout.
O'Neill joins Sunderland defender Dan Ballard, Eoin Toal, and midfielders Ali McCann and Jamie McDonnell in being ruled out of the upcoming double-header because of injury.

articles.title: Birmingham announce shock Brady departure
articles.summary: Birmingham have announced the shock departure of NFL legend Tom Brady as minority owner with the Bluenoses sitting top of the Championship table.
body: In a statement, the club said: "Birmingham City Football Club expresses its sincere gratitude to Tom Brady for his involvement with and unwavering support for the club over the last three years.

"It was truly amazing to have someone with Tom's experience and passion associated with the club, and the club looks forward to continuing to build on that foundation from the training ground to the Birmingham community."

Brady, a seven-time Super Bowl champion in his playing days, bought a minority stake in the club in August 2023 during its takeover by an American capital management firm but saw the club relegated in his first season after the surprise sacking of John Eustace.

A summer of considerable spending, including the third-tier record £15m signing of England U21 forward Jay Stansfield, saw them promoted back to the Championship at the first time of asking before the club recorded a 10th-placed finish on their first season back in the second tier.

articles.title: Sabalenka starts pursuit of WTA Finals title with opening win
articles.summary: Aryna Sabalenka got off to a winning start at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells, battling past Karolina Muchova 7-6 (7-2) 7-5, while Mirra Andreeva was also victorious in her Group 2 opener on Monday.
body: A two-time beaten finalist in the WTA Finals - including going down last year to Elena Rybakina, who stole her No 1 ranking this season - Sabalenka is looking to win the tournament for the first time.

Rybakina's late withdrawal due to a viral illness and fatigue aids Sabalenka's hopes, as does her opening victory over Wimbledon finalist Muchova, who made her sweat for it in a hugely-absorbing contest that ran six minutes shy of two hours.

Sabalenka was first to blink on serve in the first set, Muchova breaking for a 3-2 advantage, and again to lead 5-4, only for her opponent to break back immediately on both occasions - the second time when the Czech world No 7 was serving to take the opener.
Sabalenka then spurned a couple of set points in Muchova's next service game, but dominated the resulting tiebreaker, dropping just two points.
